A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisionArena. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original conversation-data analyses, expert agreement measurements, fine-tuning experiments, and offline benchmark evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations on three benchmarks and an analysis of benchmark overlap.

M1.justification: The Bradley-Terry ranking and style-control models, benchmark curation, VLM judging procedure, and Llama-3.2 fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The contamination audit is an additional analysis, without a reported change to training-data selection.

E1.justification: Table 3 expands fine-tuning evaluation from MMMU and WV-Bench to include MME, HallusionBench, and MMMU-Pro. This substantially broadens coverage to cognition/perception scores and hallucination/illusion diagnostics alongside the retained understanding and preference evaluations. Training-dataset coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 removes the untuned Llama3.2-11B-V baseline from Table 3. Llama3.2-11B-V-Instruct and Llama-3.2-Llava-Instruct remain comparators. The offline benchmark comparisons and appendix comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce MME cognition/perception scores, HallusionBench accuracy measures, and MMMU-Pro accuracy. New Section 13 specifies nearest-neighbor question-text matching with cosine similarity at least 0.8. Existing training budgets, sample counts, judging procedures, and leaderboard evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused contamination analysis comparing VisionArena-Chat questions with four benchmarks in Section 13 and Table 6. Existing style-control analyses, expert agreement checks, category validation, and failure cases are retained; the failure-case material is relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 100 bootstrap estimates for Bradley-Terry ratings and report the same 95% confidence intervals in Tables 7–8. v3 adds no repeated-run information, seed reporting, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for fine-tuning.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds results for three benchmarks, including MMMU-Pro scores of 0.27 for Llama-3.2-VisionArena and 0.12 for Llama-3.2-Llava-Instruct. Retained MMMU/WV-Bench scores are unchanged, while the untuned baseline's 41.7 MMMU entry disappears. New Table 6 reports 47 MMMU and 23 MMMU-Pro matches, with zero MME or HallusionBench matches.

T1.justification: The standard and style-adjusted Bradley-Terry objectives and variable definitions in Sections 3.2 and 4.4 are unchanged. No new mathematical assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: the three-part VisionArena resource, analyses of user preferences and failures, fine-tuning utility, and approximation of online rankings. Additional benchmark evidence supports these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 newly argues in Section 5 that fine-tuning improvements are not due to benchmark contamination, referring to the question-text audit in Section 13. v1 contains no corresponding validity argument. Existing interpretations of stylistic bias and limitations concerning domains, languages, and preference versus correctness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 13 adds reproducibility details for the overlap audit: OpenAI's text-embedding-small embeddings, nearest-neighbor cosine matching, and the 0.8 threshold. Section 3.1 clarifies the categories of moderated content. Existing model-version mappings, classification and judge prompts, training details, and access links are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the HallusionBench and MMMU-Pro references to support the expanded evaluation. Existing references and the substantive positioning against previous crowdsourced datasets and benchmarks remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Acknowledgments move into the supplement, failure cases move from Section 13 to Section 16, and Section 5's results paragraph is revised. There are limited wording and cross-reference corrections; most prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 becomes a full-width table with grouped benchmark columns, and a new contamination table is added. Figure 9 and several appendix displays are relocated, with changes to author arrangement and pagination. Existing figure artwork and plotted results are retained.

improvement.justification: The broader Table 3 evaluation strengthens evidence for fine-tuning utility, and Section 13 adds a useful initial overlap check. These gains are limited: question-text matching does not establish contamination-independent performance, and removing the untuned baseline loses a direct before-tuning comparison. Overall, empirical support improves modestly while the central study remains unchanged.
